source_text: Οὕτω ποτὲ καὶ ἡ ῥάβδος Ἀαρὼν ἐβλάστησεν, ὥσπερ ἐβλάστησε τὸ στόμα τοῦ μάρτυρος νῦν. Ἀλλὰ τίνος ἕνεκεν ἐβλάστησεν ἡ ῥάβδος Ἀαρὼν τότε; Ἐπειδὴ ὁ ἱερεὺς ἠτιμάζετο. Τίνος δὲ ἕνεκεν ἐβλάστησε νῦν τὸ στόμα τοῦ μάρτυρος; Ἐπειδὴ ὁ μέγας ἀρχιερεὺς ἐβλασφημεῖτο Ἰησοῦς ὁ Χριστός. Ὅρα πόση τοῦ θαύματος καὶ συγγένεια καὶ ὑπεροχή. Καθάπερ γὰρ ἐκείνη ἡ ῥάβδος οὐχ ἡνωμένη ῥίζῃ, οὐδὲ ἕλκουσα τὰς ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς νοτίδας, ἀλλ' ἔρημος τῆς χορηγίας οὖσα τῆς ἐκεῖθεν, καὶ τὴν καρπογόνον ἀπολέσασα δύναμιν, ἐξαίφνης καρπὸν ἔδειξεν· οὕτω δὴ καὶ ἐνταῦθα ἡ φωνὴ τῆς ῥίζης ἀποστερηθεῖσα, καὶ τὴν ἐκ τοῦ ὀργάνου δύναμιν οὐκ ἔχουσα, ἐν ξηρῷ καὶ ἀγόνῳ στόματι ἐξαίφνης ἐβλάστησεν. Ἐν τούτῳ μὲν ἡ συγγένεια, ἐν ἑτέρῳ δὲ ἡ ὑπεροχή· πολὺ γὰρ ἑκατέρου τοῦ καρποῦ τὸ μέσον. Ὁ μὲν γὰρ αἰσθητὸς ἦν, ὁ δὲ πνευματικὸς, καὶ τοὺς οὐρανοὺς ἀνοίγων αὐτοὺς τῷ τὴν φωνὴν ταύτην ἀποτεκόντι τότε. Ὑπὲρ δὴ τούτων ἁπάντων συγχαίρωμεν τῷ μάρτυρι, δοξάζωμεν τὸν ταῦτα θαυματουργοῦντα Θεὸν, μιμησώμεθα τὴν ὑπομονὴν τοῦ συνδούλου, εὐχαριστήσωμεν ὑπὲρ τῆς χάριτος τῷ Δεσπότῃ, λάβωμεν ἐκ τῶν εἰρημένων ἱκανὴν ἐν τοῖς πειρασμοῖς παράκλησιν, καὶ τὴν δύναμιν τοῦ πεποιηκότος ἡμᾶς Θεοῦ καὶ τὴν κηδεμονίαν καταπλαγέντες, τὰ παρ' ἑαυτῶν πάντα εἰσφέρωμεν, καὶ τὰ παρ' αὐτοῦ πάντως ἕψεται. Κἂν ἄνθρωποι, κἂν δαίμονες, κἂν αὐτὸς ὁ διάβολος ἡμῖν πυκτεύῃ, πλέον οὐδὲν ἔσται τοῖς πολεμοῦσιν ἡμῖν· μόνον ἂν τὴν οἰκείαν ἐπιδειξώμεθα προθυμίαν, καὶ ὅσα παρ' ἡμῶν εἰσενεχθῆναι χρὴ πάντα εἰσενέγκωμεν. Οὕτω γὰρ τὴν παρὰ τοῦ Θεοῦ ῥοπὴν ἐπισπασόμεθα ἐνταῦθα, καὶ κατὰ τὴν μέλλουσαν ζωὴν πολλῆς ἀπολαύσομεν δόξης καὶ σωτηρίας· ἧς γένοιτο πάντας ἡμᾶς ἐπιτυχεῖν, χάριτι καὶ φιλανθρωπίᾳ τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, μεθ' οὗ τῷ Πατρὶ, ἅμα τῷ ἁγίῳ Πνεύματι, δόξα, τιμὴ καὶ κράτος, εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων. Ἀμήν.
thought_title: Aaron's rod and the martyr's mouth; exhortation to imitate and trust
orientation: Chrysostom is closing the homily by comparing Romanus's tongueless speech to Aaron's rod that blossomed, then urging the congregation to imitate the martyr's endurance and trust God's help.
pass_a_gloss: Thus once also the rod of Aaron blossomed, just as the mouth of the martyr blossomed now. But for the sake of what did the rod of Aaron blossom then? Because the priest was being dishonored. And for the sake of what did the mouth of the martyr blossom now? Because the great high priest Jesus Christ was being blasphemed. See how great is both the kinship and the superiority of the wonder. For just as that rod, not united to a root, nor drawing the moisture from the earth, but being bereft of the supply from there, and having lost the fruit-bearing power, suddenly showed fruit; so indeed also here the voice, deprived of the root, and not having the power from the instrument, in a dry and barren mouth suddenly blossomed. In this is the kinship, and in another thing is the superiority; for great is the distance between each of the two fruits. For the one was perceptible, but the other was spiritual, and opening the heavens themselves for the one who produced this voice then. For all these things, then, let us rejoice together with the martyr, let us glorify the God who works these wonders, let us imitate the endurance of the fellow servant, let us give thanks to the Master for the grace, let us take from the things said sufficient encouragement in trials, and, marveling at the power and the care of the God who made us, let us contribute all things from ourselves, and the things from him will certainly follow. Even if men, even if demons, even if the devil himself fights against us, there will be nothing more for those who war against us; only if we show our own eagerness, and contribute all things that must be contributed from us. For thus we will draw to ourselves the help from God here, and in the life to come we will enjoy much glory and salvation; which may it be granted that all of us attain, by the grace and love for humankind of our Lord Jesus Christ, with whom to the Father, together with the Holy Spirit, be glory, honor, and might, to the ages of ages. Amen.

choices.why: The verb is used for both the rod and the mouth, and the parallel is central to the argument; 'blossomed' preserves the botanical image for both.
Chrysostom is drawing a family resemblance between the two wonders; 'kinship' keeps the relational sense rather than a vague 'similarity.'
The point is that the martyr's wonder surpasses Aaron's; 'superiority' states the comparison directly.
The voice is forcibly bereft of its root (the tongue); 'deprived' conveys the loss and the violence behind it.
Chrysostom calls Romanus a fellow servant to emphasize shared status with the congregation; the compound is kept literal.
In context ῥοπή means the decisive inclination or aid from God; 'help' is plain and fits the exhortation to draw God's support.

pass_b_english: In just this way Aaron's rod once blossomed, just as the martyr's mouth has blossomed now. But why did Aaron's rod blossom then? Because the priest was being dishonored. And why has the martyr's mouth blossomed now? Because the great high priest, Jesus Christ, was being blasphemed. See how great is both the kinship and the superiority of the wonder. For just as that rod was not joined to a root, nor drawing moisture from the earth, but was barren of any supply from there and had lost its fruit-bearing power, yet suddenly produced fruit—so here too the voice, deprived of its root and having no power from the organ, suddenly blossomed in a dry and barren mouth. In this lies the kinship, and in another thing the superiority: for the distance between the two fruits is great. The one was perceptible to the senses, but the other was spiritual, and it opened the very heavens for the one who brought forth this voice at that time.

For all these things, then, let us rejoice together with the martyr. Let us glorify the God who works these wonders. Let us imitate the endurance of our fellow servant. Let us give thanks to the Master for His grace. Let us take from what has been said sufficient encouragement in trials. And as we marvel at the power and care of the God who made us, let us contribute everything on our part, and what comes from Him will surely follow. Even if human beings, even if demons, even if the devil himself fights against us, there will be nothing more for those who war against us—only if we show our own eagerness and contribute everything that must be contributed from our side. For in this way we will draw God's help here, and in the life to come we will enjoy great glory and salvation. May we all attain it, by the grace and love for humanity of our Lord Jesus Christ, with whom to the Father, together with the Holy Spirit, be glory, honor, and might, forever and ever. Amen.

last_rejected.quote: there will be nothing more for those who war against us
last_rejected.source_quote: πλέον οὐδὲν ἔσται τοῖς πολεμοῦσιν ἡμῖν
last_rejected.why: Greek says enemies will accomplish nothing, not that they will receive nothing.
last_rejected.fix: those who war against us will accomplish nothing more
last_rejected.ruling: πλέον οὐδὲν ἔσται = 'there will be nothing more'; context implies enemies accomplish nothing. Within normal meaning range.

last_rejected.quote: only if we show our own eagerness
last_rejected.source_quote: μόνον ἂν τὴν οἰκείαν ἐπιδειξώμεθα προθυμίαν
last_rejected.why: μόνον ἂν means 'provided only that' or 'if only,' a condition for victory, not a restriction.
last_rejected.fix: provided only that we show our own eagerness
last_rejected.ruling: μόνον ἂν = 'only if'; 'only if we show' correctly conveys the condition. No meaning change.

last_rejected.why: πυκτεύῃ means 'boxes' or 'fights as a boxer,' a specific combat metaphor, not general fighting.
last_rejected.fix: boxes against us or contends against us
last_rejected.ruling: πυκτεύῃ means 'fight/box'; 'fights against us' is within normal range. Not a major error.
